text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Another Moslem family was evicted from Croat-held sector of Mostar on Sunday night, Bosnian police reported. The 72nd eviction this year was carried out at gun-point by an unidentified person, the report said.

- A war crimes trial for Bosnian Serb Dragan Ilic continues in (Moslem) government-held Tuzla, with more witnesses testifying he had been a deputy commander of Batkovic prison camp for Moslems during the war.

- Bosnia's new Central Bank's Governing Board is preparing a draft of law on the new currency, which, if properly endorsed by the parliament can be implemented by the end of next year, Kasim Omicevic, Bosnian member of the Governing Board said.

- Bosnia's post and telecommunications service to begin parcel shipments soon, director of postal services Emir Hajric said. Parcels will be delivered to a centre in Germany twice a week and prices will vary pending the distance, he said.
